clue.text: Some carpenters, perhaps, but not joiners, aren't very pleasant superficially.

definitions.text: Some carpenters, perhaps, but not joiners
definitions.meaning: first meaning: workers, carpenters among them, who refuse to join a union or a strike
second meaning: the crusts that form on the surface of a healing wound, not a pleasant sight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiners' looks like more woodworkers, but here it means people who join a union. A scab is a worker who refuses to.
explanation.definitionFit: Strike-breakers who stay out of the union are called scabs, and wound crusts are scabs too, an unpleasant thing to see on skin.

clue.text: Coins, as flipped in a game.

indicators.note: coins are flipped in a toss, and here the letters of the words are flipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: Coins tossed during some game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' acts on the letters of 'Coins as' and makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassino is an old card game in which cards on the table are captured by matching values.

clue.text: Probably involves squares, though called figures here.

definitions.text: Probably involves squares, though called figures here

parts.words: Probably involves squares, though called figures here
parts.note: squares are square dances, and the dancing moves, called figures, are shouted out by a caller

explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' and 'figures' sound like geometry or arithmetic, but they are dance terms: square dances, and the figures a caller calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A country dance held in a barn usually features square dancing, with a caller naming each figure.

clue.text: See 12 across
Tie in a race, at least one in a race.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ... is a broad tie, named for the dress worn at Royal ... races

definitions.text: at least one in a race
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... is the English racecourse, a meeting with several races, and read as ... it is one member of a race

explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-racing meeting near Windsor; the ascot tie takes its name from it. Split as A SCOT, the word is also one person of the Scottish race.
explanation.definitionFit: The cravat called an ascot and the racecourse called Ascot share the name, so both readings land on the same word.

clue.text: Just a drop of water, or a lot more.

definitions.text: Just a drop of water, or a lot more

parts.words: Just a drop of water, or a lot more
parts.note: a drop of water sounds tiny, but a waterfall is also a drop of water, and this one is enormous

explanation.walkthrough: 'A drop of water' suggests a single droplet; read as a fall of water, it describes the great waterfall on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous cataract is literally a place where a vast river drops, so it is a drop of water on a huge scale.

clue.text: When not on foot, I would shortly get in the circle.

indicators.note: to get in is to enter, so the shortened I would is placed inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
I'D is the short form of I would

explanation.surface: Someone who stops walking and joins a circle, perhaps in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not on foot is travelling on horseback or in a vehicle, which is riding.

clue.text: One entrance might be stone.

parts.note: a means one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doorway could be built of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Something unplanned and unpleasant leads to lying — but such a type might be expensive to cover.

definitions.text: such a type might be expensive to cover

indicators.note: one thing leading to another puts it first, so the unplanned mishap comes before the word for lying

parts.note: an accident is an unplanned, unpleasant event
prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: A mishap puts someone flat on their back, and such people cost insurers dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' means the mishap comes first and the lying second. 'Cover' is insurance cover: someone forever having mishaps is a bad risk, so their premiums are high.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who often has mishaps is costly to insure, since claims are likely.

clue.text: In the ring, they fling this in a way that's mildly terrific!

definitions.note: the definition is adverbial in sense: terrific originally meant causing terror, and the answer describes something done so as to cause fright

indicators.note: letters put together in another way are rearranged, so the clue's words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Boxers in the ring throwing punches with a ferocity that is rather alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges the letters of RING and THEY FLING together into the answer. 'Terrific' is used in its old sense, terrifying, which is why 'mildly' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific once meant terrifying, so something mildly terrific is done in a manner that scares, an alarming way.

clue.text: In making a strict diagnosis, you might consider it belonging to the stomach.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words, contained in them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of making, the word a and the start of strict

explanation.surface: A doctor making a careful diagnosis wonders whether the trouble is in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the medical adjective for anything relating to the stomach.

clue.text: Ring-maker.

parts.note: the Ring is the cycle of four operas The Ring of the Nibelung, and its composer made it

explanation.walkthrough: A ring-maker suggests a jeweller, but the Ring here is the great four-opera cycle, whose composer wrote both words and music.
explanation.definitionFit: The German composer created Der Ring des Nibelungen, the opera cycle known simply as the Ring.

clue.text: Revolving digits.

parts.note: digits are fingers and thumbs, and turning thumbs round each other idly is a familiar habit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digits' suggests numbers on a dial or counter, but they are thumbs being turned round one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiddling one's thumbs means rotating them idly around each other, so fingers and thumbs going round.

clue.text: Following exercise?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a retinue, the followers of an important person
second meaning: to exercise or drill

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests a workout that follows another; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble's train is their retinue of attendants, and athletes train by doing exercise.

clue.text: Day-old play, evidently.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, born the previous day, so one day old
second meaning: a 1946 Broadway comedy by Garson Kanin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Day-old' looks like it describes the play as stale. Read literally, someone born yesterday is one day old, and that phrase is also a famous play's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born the previous day makes someone a day old, and the phrase titles Garson Kanin's comedy.

clue.text: Asking for Juncus to get here as quickly as possible?

definitions.text: Asking for Juncus to get here as quickly as possible?

parts.words: Asking for Juncus to get here as quickly as possible?
parts.note: Juncus is the botanical genus of rushes, so an urgent request could whimsically be one placed for rushes

explanation.walkthrough: Juncus is the Latin name for the rush plant. An urgent request for delivery is a phrase that, read literally, means ordering rushes.
explanation.definitionFit: An order marked for urgent delivery is called by this name, and taken literally it is a request for the plant.

clue.text: Stand up and be counted, with less of eastern revolutionary movement.

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the words before it are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking a public stand, though less committed to some Eastern uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern revolutionary movement' looks like a political uprising; the movement is of letters, the thirteen in LESS OF EASTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up and be counted is to make one's views or presence felt, which is what insisting on one's rights involves.

clue.text: A foreigner in a little way outstanding.

indicators.note: the foreigner is put within the short way, contained by it

parts.note: ST, a little or abbreviated form of street, a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A foreigner who stands out in a small street.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable, as with salient points that stand out.

clue.text: Bedelia is made up, but certainly not as an Early Bird!

definitions.text: certainly not as an Early Bird
definitions.note: the definition describes a person, the opposite of one who rises early; the answer is a noun for someone who stays in bed

indicators.note: something made up is concocted, so the name's letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A woman called Bedelia is putting on her make-up, surely no early riser.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedelia looks like a woman's name; 'is made up' says its seven letters are reworked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A late riser who stays under the covers is the opposite of the early bird who gets up at dawn.

clue.text: A loud way to come across, and bear the expense.

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: Someone noisily turning up and paying for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for forte, Italian for loud, in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To be able to pay for something is to be able to meet its cost.

clue.text: Our present year and all our years might be proverbial.

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective standing for a noun: the answer is a proverb, the thing that is proverbial

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels the current year in the calendar
one's age is all the years one has lived

explanation.surface: This year and our whole lifetime might become the stuff of proverbs.
explanation.walkthrough: AD, for Anno Domini, is written before the present year's date.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying, a proverb, so it is the proverbial thing itself.

clue.text: See 6 down
Possibly good material for Koussevitzky.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hard-wearing twilled fabric
second meaning: ... Koussevitzky was the Russian-born conductor of the Boston Symphony Orchestra

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like it asks for music fit for a conductor; it asks for a cloth and his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable woollen cloth used for suits, and it was also Koussevitzky's first name.

clue.text: With broken outer ends, things go to pot this way.

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these two words are smashed up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Things with frayed edges fall apart and decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outer ends' looks like a description of frayed edges, but 'broken' says its nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed stops being useful, so the phrase means deteriorating, going to pieces.

clue.text: Implying too much of the type to spread and take possession.

definitions.text: Implying too much of the type
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in printing, an ... is excess type that must be carried over to the next line or page
second meaning: to ... a place is to spread over it and occupy it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' sounds like a kind of person; it is printer's type, the metal letters set into lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers overrun when the type will not fit, and invaders overrun a country they swarm into.

clue.text: A beetle couldn't be a cockroach!

definitions.text: A beetle couldn't be a cockroach!

parts.words: A beetle couldn't be a cockroach!
parts.note: this beetle is female by name, so it could never be the cock, the male bird, that the cockroach's name begins with

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an insect fact; the joke is in gender. A lady could never be a cock.
explanation.definitionFit: The red spotted beetle has a feminine name, so it is the opposite of a creature whose name begins with a male bird.

clue.text: It's due, perhaps, to be carried out.

indicators.note: perhaps says the words could be put another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something owed must now be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties are tasks that one is obliged to perform, things to be done.

clue.text: Smetana's was bartered.

parts.note: Bedrich Smetana's best-known comic opera is named for a young woman whose marriage is bargained over

explanation.walkthrough: The Bartered Bride is a Czech comic opera by Bedrich Smetana; the clue completes its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Smetana's opera is a young woman whose marriage is traded in a deal.
